title: Policy Transience Chronicle: Signal Matrix & Runbook Draft
body:
Summary:

This doc synthesizes a recent class of transient connectivity degradations we observed in multiple on-prem customer control-plane tunnels during December 2026. Symptoms looked like brief control-plane RPC timeouts followed by rapid recovery, but customer-facing dataplane flows (LLM inference traffic) experienced short-lived 5xx spikes and retry storms. The intent here is: (1) capture the signal matrix we used during triage, (2) formalize a compact runbook for recurring transients related to policy sync/egress manipulations, and (3) propose low-risk mitigations and telemetry items.

Impact:
- Affected: 7 private deployments across APAC/EMEA regions (customers A, C, F, H).
- User-visible: 1–3 minute latency/5xx spikes per incident, up to 0.8% of requests failing during windows.
- Business: customer support tickets opened for 4 deployments; no SLA breach recorded (SLO margin preserved).

Detection signals (what we saw):
- Control-plane RPC errors: eth0: TLS handshake timeouts on control-channel (conn attempts retried 3x before success).
- Fastheart: intermittent missing heartbeat samples in telemetry (controlplane.heartbeat.missed > 2 in 30s).
- Firewall counters: sudden surge in DROPPED packets from customer edge to control-plane IP on ephemeral ports.
- Policy events: kube-applier logs show near-simultaneous policy updates pushed to edge proxies (3–8 sec window).
- Dataplane: backend 5xx rate increases correlated to control-plane latency spikes, not to CPU/GPU saturation.

Signal matrix (useful for on-call checklists):
- Are control-plane TLS handshakes failing? (grafana: controlplane.tls.errors) -> yes/no
- Did heartbeat count drop? (prom: controlplane_heartbeat_missed_total) -> yes/no
- Are firewall drop counters elevated for control-plane IPs? (customer-fw: DROP/REJECT) -> value
- Were policy push events recorded within 60s prior to spike? (k8s: policy.apply.events) -> timestamp
- Is dataplane CPU/GPU normal? (node_exporter, nvml) -> values
- Are retries backing off or amplifying? (app metrics: client.retries.total) -> trend

Immediate triage timeline (representative incident 2026-12-17 03:14 UTC):
- 03:14 Observe: Alert fired - control-plane RPC error rate > 0.5%
- 03:15 Triage: Confirmed heartbeat misses and TLS timeouts to 10.0.52.14 (customer-edge)
- 03:17 Customer console shows recent policy rollout (git commit f7e2b3) at 03:12
- 03:19 Engineering remote into customer-bastion; firewall logs show 27 dropped SYNs per second to control-plane port 8443 for 90s
- 03:22 Mitigation: Temporarily relax egress rate-limiter on proxy (edge) and allow control-plane IP on incidental bitmask for ports 1024-65535 for 120s
- 03:24 Recovery: Heartbeats resume, TLS errors fall to baseline, 5xx spike terminates by 03:25
- 03:28 Post-incident: Collect traces, firewall dump, and policy diff for RCA

Hypotheses considered: 
1) Policy push created ephemeral connection storms: incremental policy changes triggered mass reconnects from proxies to control plane, leading to connection queuing on the customer's edge firewall with strict per-source conntrack limits.
2) Customer egress policing: edge QoS / rate-limiter dropped SYN/ACKs selectively under burst, causing TLS handshakes to fail and triggering retry loops.
3) Control-plane backend flakiness: unlikely given internal control-plane metrics stable and other tenants unaffected on same cluster.
4) MTU/path-MTU intermittence: checked, not present (ICMP unreachable not observed).

Root cause (post analysis):
Primary root cause is a transient conntrack exhaustion and egress rate-policing interaction on customer edge during simultaneous policy reloads. When thousands of proxies reconnect (policy re-evaluation), the customer's firewall enqueued and then dropped early handshake packets due to tight conntrack and egress bursting rules. This produced TLS handshake failures and caused the control-plane client library to enter aggressive retry behaviour for ~1–2 minutes.

Why this escaped earlier detection:
- Telemetry lacked a compact conntrack metric for customer edges; we only collected firewall accept/reject counters but not per-source conntrack state trends.
- Policy-rollout tool emitted no idempotent backoff (it pushed full policy to many proxies simultaneously rather than rolling gradually).

Mitigations implemented (short term):
- Add a temporary guard in policy rollouts: default staged-rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30s observation windows. (Done 2026-12-18)
- Console guidance: automatic preflight check to warn if customer firewall reports conntrack < 1k or if egress rate-limit present (feature flag gated).
- Emergency rollback runbook: how to temporarily open ephemeral high-ports to control-plane IPs for 2 minutes from customer edge (documented below).

Permanent actions & telemetry improvements (proposed):
- Instrument per-customer conntrack bucket trends via lightweight agent (requires customer opt-in).
- Add an edge heartbeat health export that surfaces conntrack pressure and egress policy fingerprints to the control plane (privacy-preserving hash).
- Update policy-applier to perform staggered rollouts by default with a tunable concurrency parameter.
- Add a rate-adaptive backoff to client handshake logic to avoid amplifying when facing SYN/DROP patterns.

Runbook draft: "Transient control-plane handshake failures due to conntrack/egress pressure"
(Triage steps for oncall)
1) Acknowledge alert and label incident type: "conntrack-egress-transient".
2) Pull recent policy apply events: k8s:policy.apply.events - look for >10 pushes in last 60s.
3) Check control-plane TLS error stream for peer IP and port (controlplane.tls.peer_errors).
4) Query customer firewall drop counters for that peer IP and ephemeral port range.
5) If drops correlate and customer reports heavy policy activity: request temporarily relax conntrack/timeouts or lift egress policing for control-plane IPs for short window. Provide exact ip ranges and port ranges (example below).
6) Staged rollback: revert last policy commit to previous stable hash if immediate relaxation is not possible.
7) Monitor: wait for 90s post-change, verify heartbeat and TLS errors down to baseline.
8) Post-incident capture: firewall tcpdump (60s), policy diff, client logs, prom traces; attach to JIRA.

Config snippets to provide to customers (example text to copy):
- To temporarily permit control-plane reconnections (120s window):
  - iptables: iptables -I FORWARD -p tcp -s <edge-cidr> -d <controlplane-ip> --dport 8443 -m connlimit --connlimit-above 100 -j ACCEPT
  - nftables example: nft add rule inet filter forward tcp daddr <controlplane-ip> dport 8443 ct count over 100 accept
- To increase conntrack table: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144

Monitoring checks to add (short list):
- per-customer: firewall.drop_rate{peer="controlplane"} (1m/5m)
- per-customer: conntrack_pressure{state="percent_used"} if agent present
- policy.apply.burst_rate -> alert if > 8 applies / 60s
- controlplane.tls.handshake_fail_rate -> lower threshold alert for private deployments

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Aisha: add staged-rollout as default in policy-applier (PR + feature flag) - ETA 2027-01-15
- Rafael: prototype conntrack telemetry agent and spec for opt-in - ETA 2027-02-01
- Liang: add control-plane IP exception snippets to support runbook and update customer-facing KB - ETA 2026-12-24 (done quick note)
- Priya: instrument alerting rules for handshake failure in grafana/alertmanager - ETA 2026-12-23

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to safely suggest conntrack tuning across a diverse set of customer appliances (vendor-specific behaviors)? (action: Rafael to include vendor notes)
- Should policy-applier require a signed opt-in from customer before performing full-fanout rollouts? (product discussion needed)
- Can we extend the client handshake library to use a randomized jittered backoff to avoid synchronized storms? (engineering spike)

Appendix: Observed support snippets (raw)
- policy diff (truncated): 
  - removed rule: allow 10.0.0.0/8 -> controlplane:8443
  - added rule: restrict 10.0.0.0/8 -> controlplane:8443 with egress-rate 200eps
- firewall excerpt (customer logs): "DROP tcp src=10.1.3.8 dst=52.14.22.9 sport=49212 dport=8443 flags=S rate-limit 200pps conntrack-full"
- client logs (edge-proxy): "[2026-12-17T03:14:51Z] handshake failed: SYN timed out, retrying (retry_count=2, backoff=250ms)"

Notes: This doc is intentionally concise and aimed at the oncall SRE team and support engineers handling private deployments. It's a working draft — comments welcome, especially for the staged-rollout default cadence and the exact telemetry fields we should add to the minimal agent.

End of chronicle.
